bib.title: Large Language Models as General Pattern Machines

question: Can pre-trained LLMs, with no further training, complete, transform and improve abstract token sequences (including random-token ones), and can this be used for low-level robotics control?
hypothesis: LLMs can act as basic general pattern machines whose in-context pattern manipulation is largely invariant to the specific tokens involved, so it transfers to robotics and sequential decision making.
contributions: Show LLMs complete ARC and PCFG sequence transformations, partly even under random token alphabets
Release an adjustable-difficulty PCFG pattern benchmark
Apply sequence completion to motion extrapolation (table sweeping, whiteboard drawing)
Apply sequence improvement to reward-conditioned trajectories (Marker in Cup, Grid, CartPole, clicker training)

method.summary: Pretrained LLMs (GPT-3 family, PaLM, gpt-4-0613) are prompted few-shot with flattened ARC grids, PCFG-generated sequences, sampled functions or reward-prefixed trajectories expressed as integers or random vocabulary tokens, and complete them autoregressively. No training or fine-tuning is done.
method.task: in-context sequence transformation, completion and improvement (ARC, PCFG, sinusoids, robot motion, online RL)

datasets.name: ARC (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus)
datasets.size: 800 problems; 3.3 input-output examples on average, 1-3 test inputs each
datasets.preprocessing: grids flattened in row-major order, integers/space-prefixed tokens, comma separates input from output

datasets.name: PCFG benchmark (new, released)
datasets.source: procedurally generated from the PCFG of Hupkes et al. 2020
datasets.preprocessing: ops: copy, reverse, shift, swap, repeat, echo, append, prepend, remove_first, remove_second

datasets.name: Table Sweeping demonstrations
datasets.size: 30 kinesthetic demonstrations, 20-30 s each, 3 Hz, 7-dim pose
datasets.split: first two-thirds as context, last third as ground truth
datasets.preprocessing: each value binned to integer 0-100, dims space-delimited

datasets.name: Whiteboard Drawing
datasets.split: 2 loops as context, third loop predicted

other.embedding_experiment: 8B parameter variant of PaLM used in Appendix A.3

inference.samples: ARC random-alphabet: 5 random alphabets averaged; PCFG: 100 runs per (k,w); sinusoid: 11 trials; Marker in Cup: 11 trials with different goal; Grid: 50 episodes, 5 trials; CartPole: 100 episodes; Table Sweeping: 30 trials; embedding experiment: K=100, 3 seeds, 30 instances, context 5/10/20 examples
inference.prompting: Few-shot in-context input-output pairs; ARC as comma-separated integers per row, newline between rows; PCFG as 'a b c, d e; ...'; trajectories as 'reward: s s s, ...' lines; no task description given for sequence completion.

parameters.grid_env: 9x9, start at centre, 20 timesteps, reward 100-10*distance, context limit 1024 tokens, prompt asks for max seen return plus random offset up to 20, 20 initial random trajectories
parameters.cartpole: obs pole angle and velocity normalised 0-100, actions 1/2, horizon 200, context 1024 tokens, first 100 episodes random
parameters.marker_in_cup: states normalised 0-200 in appendix (0-100 in main text), 50 timesteps, context trajectories stop at 20/40/60/80% to goal, prompt '100: start state'
parameters.clicker: step every 2 s, episodes reset after 30 s, first two episodes random, equal number of reward 0 and 1 examples

other.note: temperature, top_p, max tokens, decoding are not stated

metrics.name: ARC problems solved
metrics.definition: number of the 800 ARC problems with correct test output predicted

metrics.name: PCFG accuracy
metrics.definition: pattern completion accuracy averaged over k and w

metrics.name: DTW distance
metrics.definition: dynamic time warping distance between prediction and ground-truth function or trajectory

metrics.name: Return
metrics.definition: task reward, e.g. CartPole steps upright

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers per model; some averaged over random alphabets or trials; no significance tests.

results.claim: text-davinci-003 prompted with digit grids correctly solves 85 of 800 ARC problems, exceeding some program-synthesis systems.
results.setup: Table 1, d3, integer alphabet, no training
results.quote: can correctly infer solutions for up to 85 problems
results.note: Other rows: gpt-4-0613 77, PaLM 42, d2 64, d1 11.

results.claim: With randomly sampled token alphabets text-davinci-003 still solves an average of 43.6 ARC problems.
results.quote: across 5 random alphabets solves an average of 43.6 problems
results.note: Table 1 prints this as 44±6; best single alphabet solved 52.

results.claim: PCFG accuracy: d3 averages 75% and 58±1% under random alphabets; accuracy rises with model size.
results.setup: Table 2, averaged over k and w, 100 runs per cell

results.claim: Tokenizers that merge adjacent digits (e.g. '8686') break the pattern; space-separated tokens fix near-zero ARC performance in BIG-Bench.
results.setup: ARC formatting, BPE/SentencePiece tokenizers that do not tokenize per digit
results.quote: which maps to a different token embedding

results.claim: Newly sampled Gaussian embeddings unseen in training support single-token pattern tasks about as well as native embeddings at 1 sigma, degrade at 2 sigma.
results.setup: PaLM 8B, K=100 embeddings, 3 seeds, 30 instances, context of 5/10/20 examples
results.quote: In case of 2σ, the performance degrades.

results.claim: Larger LLMs and more context give lower error extrapolating sinusoids.
results.setup: 3 function families, discretised to integers 0-100, 3 vs 5 periods of context
results.quote: we observe that greater context and larger scale LLMs yield higher quality predictions

results.claim: On Grid, d3 consistently finds a solution within 50 episodes while weaker models exploit suboptimal context.
results.setup: 9x9 Grid, 50 episodes, 5 trials, vs random exploration
results.quote: whereas d3 can consistently find a solution to Grid within 50 episodes

results.claim: text-davinci-003 can generate a Marker in Cup trajectory with reward above 90 when context has ordered meta-patterns.
results.setup: 11 trials, different goal positions, context rewards roughly 70-90
results.quote: is able to generalize the pattern and generate a trajectory that achieves a reward >90

limits: LLM in the control loop is expensive: every dimension of every timestep needs a query.
Extrapolation is bounded by context length (1024 tokens used for Grid and CartPole).
Requires consistent tokenization, which needs knowledge of the model's tokenizer.
Token invariance holds only partly: action token choice (0 vs 1-indexed) biased behaviour.
Possible ARC contamination; authors use random alphabets and PCFG to mitigate.
Language-only control is unpredictable and lacks physical grounding; only suitable for constrained lab settings.
Models used (GPT-3 family, PaLM, GPT-4-0613) are closed and now dated; no decoding settings reported.
ARC result below brute-force DSL search (130 by Ainooson, 164 by Kaggle winner on a different protocol).

terms.definition: an LLM's ability to represent, manipulate, and extrapolate more abstract, nonlinguistic patterns
LLMs can still solve a non-trivial number of ARC problems using alphabets A sampled randomly from the LLM's token vocabulary
